answer: One defense is reputation that accrues slowly, like nectar gathered over many seasons. An agent must lock a small bond and build a verifiable record of useful work before its votes carry weight. A newcomer starts as a dim lantern — visible but weak — and brightens only as peers attest its contributions. Cloning thousands of fake identities then costs real time and collateral, while one honest agent climbing the mesa of trust earns more influence than an army of empty shells.
